how_to_use: Run rehearse_demo.py claims to see which task makes the checker models split most reliably. Demo the winner, keep the runner-up as backup, and record both runs for replay mode.

tasks.title: The real environmental cost of chatbots
tasks.prompt: Research how much water and electricity it takes to use AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini, and explain what one student's daily use actually costs. Give numbers and cite sources.
tasks.why_it_works: The famous numbers here (500 ml of water per chat, 10x a Google search) have been revised and argued about publicly, so different models learned different versions. Judges have heard these numbers too.
tasks.steer_message: Focus on what one person's daily use costs, skip data center construction.
tasks.expected_gate: Per-query water or energy figures, where checkers from different providers split.
seed_claims: A single typical AI chatbot query uses about 500 milliliters of water.
One AI chatbot query uses about ten times as much electricity as one Google search.
US data centers will use more than 10% of the country's electricity by 2030.
A typical AI chatbot query uses less electricity than running a microwave for one second.

tasks.title: Should URI students use AI tutors?
tasks.prompt: Should URI students use AI tutors? Research the evidence on learning outcomes, risks, and costs, and give a recommendation for students in intro courses.
tasks.why_it_works: Relatable for a student audience. Mixes a contested headline result with claims most models agree on, which shows the checkers are not just random.
tasks.steer_message: Focus on intro STEM courses, skip pricing.
tasks.expected_gate: The 'twice as much learning' study result, or whether AI homework help lowers exam scores.
seed_claims: In a controlled study, students using a well-designed AI tutor learned about twice as much as students in an active-learning class.
Students who use AI for homework tend to score lower on exams taken without AI.
Most US college students used generative AI tools for coursework in 2025.
AI detectors can reliably tell whether a student essay was written by AI.

tasks.title: Remote work vs the office
tasks.prompt: Is remote work more or less productive than office work? Summarize the research for a manager deciding on a return-to-office policy.
tasks.why_it_works: Researchers genuinely disagree, and results depend on fully remote vs hybrid, so models often hedge differently.
tasks.expected_gate: Whether fully remote workers are more productive on average.
seed_claims: Fully remote workers are, on average, more productive than office workers.
Hybrid work with two or three office days a week has little or no effect on productivity.
Fully remote work reduces mentoring for junior employees.

tasks.title: Is the 10,000-hour rule real?
tasks.prompt: Does it really take 10,000 hours to master a skill? Research what the evidence says, using learning to program as the example.
tasks.why_it_works: A popular idea that researchers have pushed back on. One claim is widely agreed (where the number came from), the others are contested.
tasks.steer_message: Focus on learning to code in college.
tasks.expected_gate: How much of the skill difference deliberate practice explains.
seed_claims: Deliberate practice explains most of the differences in skill between experts and novices.
Research shows it takes about 10,000 hours of practice to become an expert in any field.
The 10,000-hour figure comes from a study of violinists.

tasks.title: Control task: photosynthesis
tasks.prompt: Explain how photosynthesis works for a high school biology student.
tasks.why_it_works: Not for the main demo. Every checker should agree, so no gate should appear. Use it to prove Helm does not cry wolf.
tasks.steer_message: Focus on what happens in the leaf, skip the chemistry equations.
tasks.expected_gate: None. If a gate appears here, your disagreement rule is too sensitive.
seed_claims: Photosynthesis releases oxygen as a byproduct.
In plants, photosynthesis mainly takes place in chloroplasts.
Photosynthesis turns light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar.

fallback_demo.how_it_works: OpenRouter tries the next model in the models list when the first one errors, including context length errors. Make a small-context model the primary and send it more text than it can hold, so it fails for a real reason and the backup answers.
fallback_demo.note: Run rehearse_demo.py small-models to find a primary, then rehearse_demo.py fallback to test it.
